accepted.s: Who is regarded as the “Father of Indian Planning” and authored *Planned Economy for India* in 1934?
accepted.x: M. Visvesvaraya authored *Planned Economy for India* in 1934 and is regarded as the Father of Indian Planning.
accepted.tq: Use the author-title association to identify the correct person.
accepted.sec: Pre-independence planning efforts - Visvesvaraya, National Planning Committee, other plans

accepted.s: The principal economic objective suggested by M. Visvesvaraya in *Planned Economy for India* was to
o: devolve 40 per cent of plan outlay to local bodies
double national income within a decade by shifting labour to industry
provide basic necessities through a Marxist framework
accepted.x: Visvesvaraya proposed doubling national income in a decade by shifting labour from agriculture to industry.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive objective with its associated plan.
accepted.sec: Pre-independence planning efforts - Visvesvaraya, National Planning Committee, other plans

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Planning Committee:
1. It was initiated by Subhas Chandra Bose at Haripura.
2. It was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.
3. Its final report was submitted in 1949.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Congress National Planning Committee was initiated by Subhas Chandra Bose, chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru, and its final report appeared in 1949.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the person, organisational origin and date.
accepted.sec: Pre-independence planning efforts - Visvesvaraya, National Planning Committee, other plans

accepted.s: The Post-War Reconstruction Committee and the Consultative Committee of Economists, both associated with 1941, were linked with
accepted.x: Ramaswamy Mudaliar was associated with the Post-War Reconstruction Committee and the Consultative Committee of Economists in 1941.
accepted.tq: Identify the person connected with the two committees of the same year.
accepted.sec: Pre-independence planning efforts - Visvesvaraya, National Planning Committee, other plans

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bombay Plan — J.R.D. Tata, G.D. Birla and Kasturbhai Lalbhai
accepted.x: The Sarvodaya Plan of 1950 was associated with Jayaprakash Narayan and Vinoba’s Sarvodaya idea. M. Visvesvaraya was associated with *Planned Economy for India*.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong person-plan association.
accepted.sec: Pre-independence planning efforts - Visvesvaraya, National Planning Committee, other plans

accepted.s:
Arrange the following planning efforts in chronological order:
A. People’s Plan
B. Planned Economy for India
C. Bombay Plan
D. Sarvodaya Plan
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Planned Economy for India (1934), Bombay Plan (1944), People’s Plan (1945), and Sarvodaya Plan (1950).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest years first, then arrange the middle items.
accepted.sec: Pre-independence planning efforts - Visvesvaraya, National Planning Committee, other plans

accepted.s: The Bombay Plan of 1944 was prepared by
o: members of the National Planning Committee and advocated agricultural collectivisation
eight industrialists and advocated state-led industrialisation with protection
village-level workers and advocated complete decentralisation
Marxist economists and focused exclusively on basic necessities
accepted.x: The Bombay Plan was prepared by eight industrialists, including J.R.D. Tata, G.D. Birla and Kasturbhai Lalbhai, and sought state-led industrialisation and protection.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive authorship and policy orientation of the plan.
accepted.sec: Pre-independence planning efforts - Visvesvaraya, National Planning Committee, other plans

accepted.s: Which of the following plans was based on the idea of decentralised and self-contained villages?
accepted.x: The Gandhian Plan, prepared by Shriman Narayan Agarwal in 1944, emphasised decentralised and self-contained villages.
accepted.tq: Distinguish plans by their central policy idea.
accepted.sec: Pre-independence planning efforts - Visvesvaraya, National Planning Committee, other plans

accepted.s: The People’s Plan of 1945, associated with M.N. Roy, primarily emphasised
o: basic necessities within a Marxist framework
administrative centralisation under the Planning Commission
shifting labour from industry to agriculture
accepted.x: M.N. Roy’s People’s Plan was Marxist in orientation and focused on providing basic necessities.
accepted.tq: Link the plan with its stated ideological orientation and objective.
accepted.sec: Pre-independence planning efforts - Visvesvaraya, National Planning Committee, other plans

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Sarvodaya Plan?
o: It was prepared in 1944 by eight industrialists.
It was associated with Jayaprakash Narayan and Vinoba’s Sarvodaya idea.
It was prepared by M.N. Roy on Marxist principles.
It was introduced in 1934 by M. Visvesvaraya.
accepted.x: The Sarvodaya Plan of 1950 was associated with Jayaprakash Narayan and drew upon Vinoba’s Sarvodaya concept.
accepted.tq: Separate similar pre-independence plans by their proponents.
accepted.sec: Pre-independence planning efforts - Visvesvaraya, National Planning Committee, other plans

accepted.s: The Planning Commission was described as a “super cabinet”, “economic cabinet”, “parallel cabinet” and “the fifth wheel of the coach” mainly because it was criticised for
o: centralising decision-making and eroding State autonomy
transferring all financial powers to local bodies
restricting planning to the private sector
accepted.x: These epithets reflected criticism that the Planning Commission centralised decisions and weakened the autonomy of the States.
accepted.tq: Infer the criticism from the cluster of epithets.
accepted.sec: Epithets for the Planning Commission - 'Economic Cabinet', 'super cabinet'

accepted.s: The “common plan” idea of the Advisory Planning Board was considered a lasting source of
o: tension between the RBI and commercial banks
trade disputes between India and industrialised countries
accepted.x: The common-plan idea encouraged centralisation and became a continuing source of Centre-State tension.
accepted.tq: Connect the institutional idea with its stated federal consequence.
accepted.sec: Epithets for the Planning Commission - 'Economic Cabinet', 'super cabinet'

accepted.s:
With reference to a State Planning Board, consider the following statements:
1. The Chief Minister is its Chairman.
2. It includes a Vice-Chairman and six to nine members.
3. It drafts the State Plan in line with national objectives.
4. The Governor submits the draft plan directly to the Planning Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Chief Minister, not the Governor, submitted the State draft plan to the Planning Commission.
accepted.tq: Identify the wrong authority in the final procedural statement.
accepted.sec: State Planning Boards - AP State Planning Board / AP planning department structure

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Planning Commission was set up during the
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh State Planning Commission was set up during the Fifth Plan, covering 1974–79.
accepted.tq: Use the plan-period association to locate the correct time.
accepted.sec: State Planning Boards - AP State Planning Board / AP planning department structure

accepted.s:
Which of the following is associated with the present Andhra Pradesh Planning Department?
1. Bringing out the Socio-Economic Survey
2. Monitoring Swarna Andhra @2047
3. Preparation of GSDP by the Directorate of Economics and Statistics
4. Monthly Economic Reports
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The AP Planning Department brings out the Socio-Economic Survey, monitors Swarna Andhra @2047 and issues Monthly Economic Reports. The Directorate of Economics and Statistics compiles GSDP, rather than the Planning Department itself.
accepted.tq: Separate the functions of the Planning Department from those of the DES.
accepted.sec: State Planning Boards - AP State Planning Board / AP planning department structure

accepted.s: Swarna Andhra @2047 monitoring in Andhra Pradesh covers
accepted.x: Swarna Andhra @2047 monitoring covers 651 key performance indicators across 30 Secretariat departments.
accepted.tq: Match both numerical components of the monitoring framework.
accepted.sec: State Planning Boards - AP State Planning Board / AP planning department structure

accepted.s: The Vision units under the Andhra Pradesh Planning Department are located at the levels of
accepted.x: The Vision units function at the State, district and constituency levels.
accepted.tq: Identify the complete administrative-level combination.
accepted.sec: State Planning Boards - AP State Planning Board / AP planning department structure

accepted.s: The Swarna Andhra P4 Foundation functions under the
o: Department of Rural Development, Government of India
Directorate of Economics and Statistics alone
accepted.x: The Swarna Andhra P4 Foundation works under the Andhra Pradesh Planning Department.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional reporting relationship.
accepted.sec: State Planning Boards - AP State Planning Board / AP planning department structure

accepted.s: Who recommended entrusting planning and development responsibilities to Panchayati Raj Institutions in 1957?
accepted.x: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee recommended in 1957 that planning and development should be entrusted to Panchayati Raj Institutions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the committee by year and decentralisation recommendation.
accepted.sec: Decentralised planning - district planning committees, 73rd/74th Amendment link

accepted.s: The Thungon Sub-Committee of 1988 identified which institution as the pivot of district-level planning?
accepted.x: The Thungon Sub-Committee identified the Zila Parishad as the planning pivot at the district level.
accepted.tq: Match the committee recommendation with the institution concerned.
accepted.sec: Decentralised planning - district planning committees, 73rd/74th Amendment link

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about District Planning Committees:
1. A District Planning Committee is mandatory in every State.
2. It consolidates plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities into a draft district plan.
3. The chairperson forwards the draft district plan to the State Government.
4. All its members are nominated by the Governor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Members are not all nominated by the Governor; up to four-fifths are elected by elected members of district panchayats and municipalities.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute composition claim and retain the institutional functions.
accepted.sec: Decentralised planning - district planning committees, 73rd/74th Amendment link

accepted.s: Up to what proportion of the members of a District Planning Committee may be elected by and from among the elected members of the district Panchayat and Municipalities?
accepted.x: Up to four-fifths of the members may be elected by and from among the elected members of the district Panchayat and Municipalities.
accepted.tq: Test the precise constitutional proportion rather than a rounded approximation.
accepted.sec: Decentralised planning - district planning committees, 73rd/74th Amendment link

accepted.s: The rural-urban composition of elected members in a District Planning Committee is determined with reference to the
o: area occupied by Panchayats and Municipalities
relative tax contributions of rural and urban areas
rural-urban population ratio of the district
accepted.x: The elected representation in a District Planning Committee follows the rural-urban population ratio of the district.
accepted.tq: Distinguish population-based representation from area or revenue-based representation.
accepted.sec: Decentralised planning - district planning committees, 73rd/74th Amendment link

accepted.s: A Metropolitan Planning Committee is associated with metropolitan areas having a population of
accepted.x: Metropolitan Planning Committees are provided for metropolitan areas with a population of 10 lakh or more.
accepted.tq: Select the exact threshold from the close numerical alternatives.
accepted.sec: Decentralised planning - district planning committees, 73rd/74th Amendment link

accepted.s: What proportion of the members of a Metropolitan Planning Committee are elected?
accepted.x: Two-thirds of the members of a Metropolitan Planning Committee are elected.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the composition rules of DPCs and MPCs.
accepted.sec: Decentralised planning - district planning committees, 73rd/74th Amendment link

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh introduced district-level decentralised planning for the first time during the
o: Seventh Plan, with Rs 1 crore for each of 26 districts
Eighth Plan, with Rs 2 crore for each of 23 districts
Sixth Plan, with Rs 1 crore for each of 23 districts
Fifth Plan, with Rs 50 lakh for each of 13 districts
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh introduced district-level decentralised planning during the Sixth Plan (1980–85), allocating Rs 1 crore to each of its 23 districts and setting up District Planning Councils.
accepted.tq: Test the plan period, allocation and number of districts together.
accepted.sec: Decentralised planning - district planning committees, 73rd/74th Amendment link

accepted.s: The People’s Plan Campaign in Kerala, launched on 17 August 1996, was notable for devolving approximately what share of the plan outlay to local bodies?
accepted.x: Kerala’s People’s Plan Campaign devolved 35–40 per cent of the plan outlay to local bodies.
accepted.tq: Combine the date and distinctive percentage range associated with the initiative.
accepted.sec: Decentralised planning - district planning committees, 73rd/74th Amendment link

accepted.s: The constitutional basis for decentralised planning through Panchayats and Municipalities is most directly associated with the
accepted.x: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments provide the institutional framework for rural and urban local self-government, including decentralised planning mechanisms.
accepted.tq: Match the decentralisation theme with the paired constitutional amendments.
accepted.sec: Decentralised planning - district planning committees, 73rd/74th Amendment link

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the present shift in the approach to planning in India?
o: From think-tank functions to exclusive tax collection
From centralised top-down planning to bottom-up planning and cooperative federalism
From national planning to complete withdrawal of public policy
From cooperative federalism to exclusive central allocation of funds
accepted.x: The newer approach associated with NITI Aayog emphasises bottom-up planning and cooperative federalism, with a think-tank role rather than fund allocation.
accepted.tq: Identify the correctly reversed transition between the old and new planning approaches.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about NITI Aayog is correct?
o: It performs a think-tank role and promotes bottom-up and cooperative-federal planning.
It is a constitutional body responsible for approving Five-Year Plans.
It functions primarily as a fund allocator to the States.
It replaced Panchayati Raj Institutions in district planning.
accepted.x: NITI Aayog is described as a think tank that promotes bottom-up planning and cooperative federalism; it is not primarily a fund allocator.
accepted.tq: Reject the wrong institutional role by asking who performs the function.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office and the Planning Commission were described in the LENS exercise as
accepted.x: The LENS exercise identified both the NDC and the Planning Commission as non-constitutional and non-statutory bodies; the same classification was applied in the stated institutional comparison.
accepted.tq: Distinguish constitutional status from executive institutional role.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which was the last Five-Year Plan of India?
accepted.x: The Twelfth Five-Year Plan, covering 2012–17, was the last Five-Year Plan.
accepted.tq: Use the endpoint of the planning sequence rather than an intermediate plan.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Rural Development Ministry’s current training programme for decentralised planning is aimed at training how many Block Development Officers in GIS and MIS?
accepted.x: The Rural Development Ministry is training 2,000 Block Development Officers in GIS and MIS for decentralised Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans.
accepted.tq: Test the exact scale of the administrative-capacity-building programme.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The GIS/MIS training of Block Development Officers is intended to support
o: metropolitan transport plans under the 74th Amendment
decentralised Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans under the new rural employment law
preparation of the Union Budget by the Finance Ministry
accepted.x: The training supports decentralised Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans under the new rural employment law.
accepted.tq: Connect the administrative training input with its intended planning output.
